newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian stock exchange starts trading.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian stock exchange starts trading.

text.p: Palestinians launched a stock market on Tuesday in the West Bank town of Nablus.
Officials said 23 companies had already been listed on the exchange for trading and that 20 others were in the process of being listed.
"This is an exciting moment. In fact I can see my wife in the background shedding a drop or two of tears," said Safwan Bataina, Palestine Securities Exchange general manager.
The first two transactions were shown on a screen at the bourse moments after the exchange was officially opened.

Officials of the exchange broke into applause when a screen flashed the completion of the first transaction -- 100 shares of the Arab Insurance Co sold for four Jordanian dinars ($5.60) each. By close, the company's share had risen to 4.07 dinars.
A smaller transaction followed of 10 shares in the Arab Real Estate Co, which were sold for 11 dinars each.

Bataina said the exchange would hold one weekly trading session during an introductory phase which will last a few weeks. Regular trading, with several sessions per week, would begin as trading volume builds up, he said.
Trading was being conducted in the dinar or the dollar, depending on the currency the company was capitalised at.
Bataina said that while trading today was done at the bourse, it would be conducted from the brokerage offices across the West Bank starting from the third session in two weeks' time.
Daily market data would be published and a market index, to be called the Jerusalem Index, would be added after the introductory phase, Bataina said.
"We also provide conditions for easy, liquid, transparent trading and which will lead to the discovery of real prices that will reflect the true value of the company in concern," he said.
They estimated that there were some 60 joint-stock companies in the West Bank and Gaza Strip with estimated combined market capitalisation of $700 million eligible for listing.
The $2 million electronic bourse was set up to help attract long-term investment from expatriate Palestinians.
Brokerage firms said that investors from Jordan and Israel began making inquiries about investing through the exchange.
Jamal Aladdin, general manager of the Jordan and Palestine Financial Investment Co, said he had received inquiries from two Israeli brokerage firms on Tuesday.

"This exchange is very important because its launching comes at a time when our economy is overcoming problems and entering the phase of development," Palestinian Finance Minister Mohammed Zuhdi al-Nashashibi said moments before the opening.

Nashashibi said Israeli closures on the West Bank and Gaza Strip that impede trade remained a threat to the Palestinian economy and the exchange. He said Palestinian negotiators were pressing the Jewish state to end the closures.

Four brokerage firms based in Nablus and Ramallah are registered to do business at the exchange. Traders and brokers have undergone training at the bourse. Jordan-based Arab Bank is the clearing house for trading.
Before now, informal trading in some West Bank and Gaza companies was carried through money changers or through the company whose shares were being traded.
